16febh-playful-feedback-toggle-buttons.summary:
A light-gray canvas (#f1f1f1) holds one centred pair of feedback buttons. Together they look like a pill split in two by a 12 px gap: the left half (thumbs-up) runs x 174–354 and the right half (thumbs-down) runs x 366–546, both y 294–426. Each half is 180×132. Its outer end is a full semicircle (radius ~66) and its inner corners are only slightly rounded (~8 px). The fill is an off-white #f7f7f7 with a hairline gray border and a soft drop shadow underneath. Each half holds a solid black glyph about 60 px across. The thumbs-up points up and right; the thumbs-down is its mirror. A black macOS-style arrow cursor with a white outline acts out four clicks:
1. **Like on, ~0.45s.** The left half shrinks to about 0.9 scale. From 0.65s to 0.95s the glyph turns dark green, grows to about 2× and leaps up out of the button, its top reaching y≈203. Meanwhile a mint radial glow fills the button.
2. **Glyph lands, 1.0–1.25s.** The glyph drops back, turns bright green (#0dbc39) and settles on the glow.
3. **Like off, ~1.85s.** The button shrinks again. The glyph darkens to deep green, then black, and the glow fades. The button is neutral by 2.35s.
4. **Dislike on, ~2.95s.** The cursor moves to the right half and clicks. The button shrinks, and from 3.05s to 3.35s the glyph goes dark red, then bright red (#e5173f). It wobbles in place (it does not fly), and a pink radial glow fills the button.
5. **Dislike off, ~4.15s.** A second click darkens the red glyph back to black and clears the glow. Everything is neutral by 4.6s.

The only moving parts are the cursor, the press scale, the glyph colour, scale and position, and the glow.

1b68k7-bee-garden-progress-slider.summary: A single slider centred on a flat near-black stage (#181818, 1480x720). Across the top runs a header row: "Garden" on the left (x 209, baseline about y 222, ~24px regular sans, light grey) and a percentage on the right, right-aligned at x 1262, the same size but dimmer grey. About 225px below sits a thin dark-grey track (#262626, ~4px tall, rounded ends) from x 232 to about x 1238. A thicker sage-green fill (#6b8f6a, ~6px, rounded caps) grows from x 232 to the drag position. Along the fill a flat-illustrated garden grows: a row of short grass tufts on the line, and flowers on thin green stems with leaf pairs, up to ~150px tall (tops near y 282): yellow tulip, coral poppies with dark centres, white daisies with yellow centres, purple lavender spikes, blue forget-me-not clusters, pink round blooms with dark centres, pink tulips, lilac asters, a pink dahlia. A bee emoji (~40x45) sits on the line at the leading edge of the fill as the thumb and follows the pointer with a little lag. Motion is the cursor dragging: going right, the fill and the number rise together, bare stems shoot up just ahead of the bee and their heads open a beat later, left to right. Going left, the fill shrinks, the flowers past the thumb drop their petals, which scatter up and to the right and fade over ~0.5s, and the stems shrink back down. The clip goes 3% → 34% (0–2.5s), → 68–69% (~3.9–4.5s), back to 24% (~4.6–5.7s, with petals scattering), jumps to 100% (~5.9–6.6s; the whole row sprouts as bare stems, then blooms), drags back to ~70% (~7.2–9.3s), then forward to 98% by 12s.

14scng-flashnet-network-landing-page.summary: A light hero (#fcfcfc) sits above a pale grey band (#f7f7f7, y 958–1080). On the left, starting at x=288, is a two-line headline at about 60px: "The network of networks." in near-black, with "Flashnet unifies everything." in mid-grey (#7a7a7a) below it. Lower down is a 3-line grey body paragraph (y≈693–757) and a flat light-grey "Read the docs" button (289,793,130,38). The right side holds a network diagram drawn in perspective. A small white disc carrying the black Flashnet bolt logo sits at about (1437,866). Thin pale-mint spokes radiate from it, and faint mint concentric ellipses surround it. Four 3D rounded-square chain tiles sit on an arc above the disc: a front slot at (888,540), then (1143,453), (1443,420) and (1742,456), each tile tilted in perspective and casting a soft drop shadow. A bright mint double line runs from the upper left, through the front tile, to the centre logo. A small white pill label above the front tile names the chain. About every 4s the tiles rotate one slot counter-clockwise along the arc, which takes about 0.35s (at 1.75–2.15, 5.8–6.15 and 9.8–10.1). The old front tile fades to grey and drops down-left out of view, a new tile slides in from the right edge, and the label disappears and then comes back with the new name: Ethereum → Lightning → Solana → Tron. During each hold, mint rings pulse outward from the centre disc, short mint dashes travel along the spokes, and the label appears about 1.5–2s after the tiles settle. The text, button and centre logo never move.

1yi26a-accordion-faq-interaction.summary: A single centred FAQ section on a warm off-white page (soft vertical gradient #f1eee7 at top to #e2ded5 at the bottom). At the top sits a bold, dark, centred title "Frequently asked questions" (~40px) with a grey subtitle beneath it. Below, the FAQ list is drawn as a red piano accordion about 773px wide, centred on x=717. Its top is a red-marble panel holding a 15-white-key, 10-black-key piano keyboard in a black frame. Five white question cards (730×58, radius ~10, pitch 65px) act as the bellows. Grey metallic chevron pleats and small silver rod pins stick out on both sides of each card. The bottom is a red-marble panel with a cream trapezoid button board (4 rows × 12 black spherical buttons, one marked with a white diamond), silver corner caps, and a dark leather strap handle below. A soft shadow sits under the whole instrument. The instrument stays vertically centred, so the title moves up whenever the instrument grows. Motion: (1) 0.4–0.85s: the instrument opens from a closed state, where the bellows are 5 blank 14px strips, to five labelled cards. The title rises ~58px. (2) 2.05–2.35s: the cursor grabs the handle and drags it down. The gaps between cards stretch (pitch 65→~89) and the bottom edge moves ~+114px. On release at ~2.5s it snaps shut past rest (−187px at 2.82s), springs back with an overshoot (+55 at 2.98s) and settles by 3.35s. (3) Clicking a card opens it: 'Do you offer refunds?' at ~3.8s, 'Can I cancel anytime?' at ~4.5s and 'Can I change my plan later?' at ~5.3s. Each card grows from 58 to ~88px and shows a grey answer line. Its plus twists into a minus over ~0.3s. One or two piano keys go down (tinted beige) as a chord plays. At 5.45s a small white pill reading "E minor 7" with a red note icon appears. (4) From 9.15 to 10.25s the three cards close again in reverse order, one about every 0.5s. Around 11–12s the cursor presses piano keys. (5) At 13.25s there is another stretch drag, then at ~14s a collapse to the closed state. It reopens at 14.8–15.25s. Throughout, the red marble texture slowly flows even at rest.

i61wwn-painterly-finance-app-onboarding.summary: A single portrait phone screen (315x685, about 36px corner radius) sits centred on a near-white #fdfdfd canvas. A classical oil-painting landscape fills the whole screen: pale beige-green sky, a tall dark-green tree on the right with a red-brown trunk, a lilac hill, and yellow-green foliage at the bottom. Over the painting sit large concentric glass lens rings. They are centred low on the screen behind the spinner at about (812,650) and are about 104px apart. Each ring refracts and smears the painting at its bright rim, and the rings run off the left and right edges of the screen. In the lower third is a frosted, translucent rounded card (277x158, radius about 16). Its top-centre carries a small, slightly lighter translucent disc (about 68px) holding a static white 9-spoke spinner with a dark centre dot. Below it are three centred lines of small white body copy. At the bottom, 16px above the screen edge, is a white pill button reading "Get Started" in dark medium type. Only one thing moves: the lens rings ripple outward from the centre continuously and evenly. A ring's top edge rises at about 50px/s along the centre column (382 to 357 between 5.95s and 6.45s), so a new ring spawns about every 2s, and the look repeats about every 12s (6.45s ≈ 18.5s). The painting itself, the card, the spinner, the text, the button and the phone frame all stay perfectly still.

dkolso-self-building-website-cursors.summary: A 30 s screen recording on a near-white canvas (#f7f9fb). From 0 to about 3.4 s, 18 small coloured cursor arrows (purple, red, salmon, orange, yellow, green, teal, sky and blue) orbit loosely around a pale grey rounded-square "S" logo (#d7dae0, 920,491,80×93) at frame centre. The ring stays about 330 px wide (x≈750–1160, y≈340–720) and keeps reshuffling into arcs. Each cursor is a filled arrowhead about 18 px across with a white outline and a soft shadow. A black system pointer sits still near the top right (≈1780,165). At about 3.45 s the scene becomes a design-tool canvas: a dark ruler band runs along the top (0–27 px) and the left edge, with blue selection boxes, size badges ("580 × 130", "53 × 20"), dotted guides and two red vertical guides at x≈261 and x≈1120–1141. The cursors build a SaaS landing page called "Swarm". They type the text letter by letter with I-beam cursors, draw boxes with crosshair and pen cursors, duplicate placeholder "Product" and "agent/research" labels, then retype them into their final words. The finished hero (rulers gone by 7.8 s) has: a nav bar (Swarm logo, the links Product / Agents / Docs / Pricing, and a black "Get access" button); a two-line 80 px headline, "Run a thousand agents as one."; a grey subline; a black "Start building" button and a white "Read the docs" button; and on the right a dark "swarm.dispatch(task)" panel above a 2×2 tree of four white agent cards, a blue progress bar about 65 % full, and a mono caption. A "Used by teams at" row of five wordmarks sits in a 224 px grid. After 8.35 s the page scrolls up in steps and the cursors keep building the next sections: "Built for running agents in production." with a 3×2 grid of feature cards (duplicated as "Smart routing", then retyped), "One file describes the whole swarm." with a dark swarm.yaml code window, a stats row ("10k+ 38ms 99.99% 0"), "How a task moves through Swarm." (Define / Dispatch / Converge), and "Priced by the size of your swarm." with a "$0" plan card. Thin light-grey grid lines frame every section, and a red vertical guide at x≈261 stays visible throughout the build.

ewfwo2-tooltip-hover-delay-comparison.summary: A light, quiet comparison demo on a #f4f4f4 page: two identical white cards stacked (top [48,48,1344,480], bottom [48,552,1344,480], ~40px corner radius). Each card has a handwritten-script title at top-left ("Delay on every hover" in magenta, "Delay once, then instant" in mint green), a grey "N.Ns waiting" counter at top-right, a centred floating white formatting toolbar (691x78, ~18px radius, soft drop shadow) holding Body▾ | B I U S | link code quote | a coloured dot (magenta on top, mint on bottom), and a full-width 10px grey timeline track near the card bottom. Only one card is active at a time; the other sits at ~30% opacity. 0–7.8s the top card runs: an arrow cursor enters, turns into a pointing hand, and hovers B, I, U, S, link, code, quote left to right (~0.9s per button). Each hover shows a light-grey hover square, a small blue spinner ring plus a light-blue pill counting down "500ms"→"0ms" beside the cursor, then a near-black tooltip ("Bold ⌘B", "Italic ⌘I", …) fades in above the button; the previous tooltip lingers grey as it fades out. The waiting counter climbs 0.5s per button to 3.5s and the timeline paints one ~83px blue segment per wait, leaving seven segments and a "6.9s" label that rides the timeline's end. At ~7.8s the top card dims and the bottom card wakes: the same sweep happens, but only the first hover (B) waits 500ms; every later tooltip appears instantly in solid black with "0ms". Its counter stops at 0.5s and its timeline holds one blue segment with the label ending at "3.7s". Around 13.4–14.2s the top card fades back to full, so the clip ends holding both cards side by side: 3.5s/6.9s vs 0.5s/3.7s.

y9mnpy-sheet-animation-keyframe-explorat.summary: A near-black canvas (#0f100d) split into two columns. On the left, a monospace code editor with no chrome: 18 right-aligned line numbers (x≈108–140) and CSS code starting at x=192, line pitch ≈51 px, type ≈30 px. The code is `@keyframes sheet-in { 0% { transform: translateY(100%); opacity: 0; } 60% { transform: translateY(-4%); opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: translateY(0%); } } .sheet { animation: sheet-in 500ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); }`. Only the lines inside a "focus band" are legible. The band is marked by two blue dotted rules running x=78→975. Inside it, line numbers turn blue, property names are bold off-white, values are grey and numbers/percentages are blue. Every line outside the band is shown as dim, scrambled random characters. As the band moves, characters scramble and then decode into real code. A white up/down resize cursor drags the band's edge. On the right, a phone outline (1050,83, 329×922, radius ≈60, grey 2 px stroke) holds six grey placeholder bars and two faint dotted guide lines at y≈447/468. Between the editor and the phone, a thin vertical timeline ruler at x≈1008 (y 238→648, end caps and a middle tick) carries a short blue dash that shows the scrub position. A second short blue dash at x≈1388–1404, right of the phone, tracks the sheet's top edge. A bottom sheet (308 px wide, rounded top, light-grey outline, #151614 fill, grabber bar, one bright title bar and two grey bars) is driven by the band. With the band on the 0% block the sheet is hidden. When the band is dragged to the 60% block (≈2.05–2.75 s) the sheet slides up from below to top≈449, overshooting. On the 100% block and `.sheet` rule (≈4.8–6.3 s) it settles to top≈467. The band then scrubs back and forth (7.85–9.05, 10.05–11.2, 11.55 s) with the sheet tracking 449–467. Finally (13.0–13.75 s) the band jumps back to the 0% block and the sheet slides back down out of the phone.

1knz9n-hamster-cookie-consent-modal.summary: A single white cookie-settings card (x180–540, y104–615, ~24px corner radius, very soft wide grey shadow) sits centred on a flat #efefef page. Inside, top to bottom and centred on x=360: a bold near-black title "Cookie settings" (~26px, y≈147), a grey subtitle "Every cookie you accept goes to the hamster" (~13px, y≈172), a painterly hamster illustration (~224×218, x248–472, y193–411) on a barely-off-white square, then three settings rows (Analytics y≈445, Marketing y≈483, Personalization y≈521) separated by 1px hairlines from x209 to x511, each with a label at left (~15px, dark) and a 39×23 pill toggle at right (x472–511): off = light grey track with a white knob at left, on = green #22c55e-ish track with the white knob at right. A mouse cursor drives the story: at ~0.9–1.1s it clicks the Analytics toggle, which slides on and launches a ~50px chocolate-chip cookie from the toggle that arcs left to below the hamster (~1.18s), into its paws (~1.43s) and up to its mouth (~1.7s); the hamster nibbles it (~2.2–2.75s) and its face turns from a sad frown to a content smile (~3.15s). 1ipk9s-flyingpress-bento-feature-grid.summary:
A light, centred feature section on a near-white #f2f2f4 page. At top centre is a small white pill eyebrow, "Why FlyingPress" (y≈67–97). Below it is a large near-black headline, "Real-time WordPress optimization" (≈48px, tight tracking, y≈112–160), and a one-line grey subtitle (y≈184). Under these sits a 3×2 bento grid of white cards, each 360×382 with ≈20px radius and 15px gutters (columns x=45/420/795, rows y=234/631). The upper part of each card is an illustration on a soft peach-to-orange wash, some with a faint dotted texture. Each card ends with a 20px dark title and two lines of 14px grey body text at the bottom left. The whole thing runs on a 6 s loop with 2 s beats:
(1) "Easy to Use": a FlyingPress plugin card. It shows "Active" with an orange "✓ Optimized" button and three green-checked chips until ≈2.3s. It then flips to "Inactive" / "Optimize my site" with empty-circle chips. A cursor glides onto the button at ≈3.9s and clicks it at ≈4.4s; the label blurs, and by ≈5s it is back to Active.
(2) "Fewer Settings": three toggle pills (Page Caching, Image Optimization, Critical CSS). They switch off and on, collapse into a single stacked "All optimizations" pill at ≈2.5–4.3s, then fan back out with all three on.
(3) "Core Web Vitals": three metric pills (CLS, LCP, INP) with ring gauges and Good/Poor/Needs-work badges. The middle pill is enlarged. Every ≈2s (at 0.4, 2.45, 4.4, 6.4) the list scrolls up one pill, and the ring values count and recolour.
(4) "All in One": a large white arch cut into the orange wash. Faint app-icon tiles sit behind it and fade in and out, with a glossy orange FlyingPress app icon at the bottom of the funnel.
(5) "Great Support": an orange user avatar centred in concentric peach rings, with three small white icon bubbles (?, headset, cursor) orbiting it clockwise.
(6) "Compatibility": a glossy FlyingPress icon in the middle row between a cloud tile and a "+" tile. The top row of logo tiles (W, Kinsta, grid logo) slides left and the bottom row (Elementor, cloud, +) slides right as a continuous marquee.
The header and the card frames never move.

1l9xq0-ascii-shark-ai-chat.summary: A light, near-white chat landing page (#fafafa) covered by a faint ruled grid of character cells (about 10 px wide by 14.6 px tall), with a 1 px grey hairline along the top and an 11 px warm-grey band (#dddbd6) across the bottom. Everything is centred on one column. At the top sits a small frosted 'History' pill [522,15,130,46] with a clock-with-arrow icon, grey label and a down chevron, plus a soft drop shadow. In the middle a large, light, thin-weight sans heading reads "what’s on your mind?" (about 60 px, near-black, x 322–852, baseline near y 490). Just below it is a wide frosted-glass prompt bar [205,524,765,110] with a radius of about 12, a 1 px light border and a translucent grey fill. It holds the placeholder "Ask haj anything...", a + icon and a mic icon at the bottom left, the monospace hint "↵ send · ⇧↵ newline" at the bottom right, and a 38 px grey square send button with a ↗ arrow. A big blurred grey haze (#e1e2de at its centre) spreads behind the heading and bar. Behind all of it, several sharks drawn as ASCII text art swim through the frame for the whole 24.5 s. Some are brown-and-cream leopard sharks and some are blue-grey hammerheads. Each shark is built from axis-aligned grid tiles: a grey-to-black square with a light monospace glyph (S % X 8 @ t : #), plus a few tinted tiles (violet, green, orange). Faint dotted fins and 'o' bubbles trail them. The tiles snap to the grid as a shark moves, so shapes re-raster cell by cell instead of rotating. A shark that passes behind the prompt bar turns into a soft blurred smudge (backdrop blur), and inside the haze it fades lighter. Sparse small dark '-' dashes sit in grid cells, clustered left of the bar and scattered elsewhere, and they flicker and drift as the sharks pass. The UI (pill, heading, bar, button) never moves. From 0 to about 9 s, three or four sharks circle the centre. From about 9.5 to 14 s they leave toward the top-right and bottom-left corners and the centre is empty. From about 14 s, hammerheads come back in from the right and cross over the heading and bar until the end.

bwl3yk-paper-fold-portfolio-page.summary: A single-column personal portfolio drawn as one sheet of off-white paper (#fcfcfc). The sheet sits in a light grey surround (#f2f2f2) and has a scalloped postage-stamp edge on all four sides, inset about 25px from the frame. On the sheet, left column: a small scalloped stamp sticker (about 157px) with a crayon drawing of a red house, blue scribbles, green grass, "4:00", "NYC", "Jm.SV" and ":)". The text column starts at x≈524 and holds, top to bottom: the handwritten all-caps name "JAMES CLEMENTS"; a three-line sans-serif bio (~29px, near-black) with underlined links "Vercel" and "Old Friends"; a grey handwritten label "WRITING"; and one row with "SKILLS ARE SOFTWARE" (black handwritten, light grey underline) on the left and a grey "OCT 5" on the right at x≈1156. The cursor grabs edges and corners of the sheet and peels them back like real paper. The folded flap shows a white underside with a soft grey gradient shadow along the crease. Its scalloped edge is drawn as three stacked offset copies (blue, green, red), which reads as a misregistered print. Under the sheet is a second page: a 3×2 grid of ~300px scalloped light-grey tiles, each with a grey "?" except the top-left tile, which holds the same stamp drawing at about twice the size. 16430q-drag-shift-file-converter.summary: A screen recording of a macOS desktop with a warm wallpaper (red at left, yellow at top centre, brown at top right, lilac and purple at bottom right). It opens on a MacBook seen at an angle against white, with the menu bar and a column of desktop icons on the right. The camera pushes in until the desktop fills the frame (0–1.85s). The file "Page 001.pdf" is dragged with Shift held, and a frosted-glass radial ring opens around the cursor: a translucent peach disc with a pale gold rim, four rounded segments (DOCX top, JPG right, PNG bottom, TXT left) and a pill in the centre that names the hovered target. The hovered segment turns solid red-orange with white type. A drag ghost with a green "+" badge and a blue name tag follows the cursor. Dropping on JPG puts "Page 001.jpg" next to the PDF (~3s). Dragging the JPG opens an 8-segment image-format ring (PNG, WEBP, HEIC, TIFF, AVIF, BMP, PDF, DOCX), which then swaps to a 7-segment action ring with line icons (COMPRESS, METADATA, EDIT, ANNOTATE, ADD BG, CROP, REDACT; centre pill "1.2 MB"). Choosing CROP zooms into a "Crop Image" sheet (6–7s): a tall rounded panel with a gradient from yellow-orange to salmon, a white page with a red crop rectangle and corner handles over a grey dimmed area, an aspect-ratio segmented control (Free active in red), W/H fields, Reset and a red Apply. The crop box slides down about 45px (8.05→8.55s). The cropped JPG lands on the desktop, is dragged again through the format and action rings (11–13.5s), and ADD BG opens an "Add BG" panel (14–14.5s) with a gradient preview card, two rows of swatches, Padding/Corners/Shadow sliders, a Ratio control and a red "Save with Background" button. Padding grows from 160 to 368 to 609 px and the card shrinks inside its gradient. The panel closes, and the clip ends on a row of four desktop files ending in "Page 001 Cropped With Ba...ound.png" (from ~18s). Type is SF Pro throughout: dark grey bold uppercase on the segments, white bold on the blue name tags.

104rht-menubar-ac-control.summary: A macOS menubar strip (light grey sky, 0–55px) runs across the top of a full-bleed mountain photo. It holds a purple active-app pill, a dot, an AC icon with "16°", volume, battery, control-centre icons and "Mon 12". At 0.3–0.6s a dark navy rounded panel (~[83,78,678,948], radius ~44px) fades in under the AC menubar item and scales up from ~0.97. A small tail notch points up at the item (x≈421). The panel holds, top to bottom: a row with a thermometer icon, "Room 25°C" and a status dot; a round blue glowing power button top right; a white glossy wall-AC unit showing "16 •"; airflow made of curved blue lines and a row of 10 slanted dashes; a big light thin "16" with a blue "°C" and an "Eco Mode" pill with a toggle on the right; a temperature slider (− button, dark tick track with a white rounded-square thumb, + button, "16°" and "30°" labels); and four rounded tiles, Mode/Cool, Fan speed/Low, Sleep/Off and Airflow/L1, each with a blue icon and a chevron. Type is SF-like: light grey labels and bold white values. The fan icon, airflow lines and status dot (green↔blue) loop for the whole clip. Sequence: from ~1.4–2.3s a grab-hand cursor drags the thumb to 30. The track fills with a blue→orange gradient, the digits roll with blur, the AC reading and menubar turn to 30 in orange, and the panel warms to rust brown. At ~3.9–4.7s the thumb is dragged back to 16 and the panel cools to navy by ~5.1s. Eco Mode toggles on at ~6.5s (blue track, green leaf) and off at ~8.2s. At ~9.3s the Airflow tile gets a blue outline and opens a dark list: "Swing", L1 ✓, L2–L5, "Off". At ~10.8s Swing is chosen, the list fades out, the tile reads "Swing", Room changes to "24°C", and the bottom dash row starts swaying side to side.

Shaking the window (2.7–7.15s) splashes the water into separate blobs with bright foam rims and knocks the digits about. At ~7.4–7.55s the view goes back to full frame. 1r2vit-generative-ui-map-card.summary: A light chat transcript on an off-white #fafaf9 page, in one centred column about 897 px wide (x 286–1183). Top right is a user bubble, a light grey pill (#f4f4f3, radius ~24) with the 2-line prompt "Find me a quiet café near the park where I can work for a few hours." in 20px dark Inter-like type. Below it, the assistant reply in 20px dark type has bold "Linden Park." and "The Boathouse,". Under that sits a 897×538 map card with radius ~24: a grey street grid (#efeeeb blocks, white streets) rotated about -8°, a green park "Linden Park" with darker blob-shaped tree clusters, a blue oval "Linden Lake" with a green island, a small pond, and white footpaths. White pill labels mark three cafés: "Fern & Fig 4 min", "The Boathouse 5 min" and "Lumen Coffee 9 min". The selected label turns into a dark pill (#222), and a blue route runs to it from a blue "you" dot with a halo. A round theme button sits at the card's top right. Inset at the bottom of the card is a white place card: photo thumbnail, name, star rating, category · walk time, three icon+feature chips, a "‹ n / 3 ›" pager and a pale blue "Send to iPhone" pill. The follow-up line "Want to stay on the city side? Fern & Fig is closest, and Lumen Coffee has the fastest Wi-Fi. Tap one on the map to compare." sits below the card. Motion, in order: the user bubble is present from 0s. From ~0.7s the reply streams in word by word with a blurred, fading leading edge. Around 1.8–2.4s the map fades and settles in. Near 2.5–3s the pins pop in, the blue route draws to The Boathouse and the place card fades up. At ~5.0–5.15s the camera zooms in about 1.15× with motion blur. The cursor pages the place card 1/3 → 2/3 → 3/3 (Boathouse → Fern & Fig → Lumen Coffee); the selected pin goes dark and the route redraws each time. At ~9.45–9.55s the camera zooms back out after Fern & Fig is tapped on the map. From ~10s the theme button expands into a white swatch tray of 5 swatches with a name label. Clicking them recolours the whole map: Vivid, a muted sage "Earth", "Autumn" (orange trees, beige ground, orange route), a desaturated grey winter, and "Night" (dark grid, dark-green park). Returning to Vivid at ~16.5s happens as a circular reveal that grows from the clicked swatch across the dark map. The tray collapses back into the button. At ~18.3s the camera zooms toward the bottom-right; the cursor clicks "Send to iPhone", which shows "Sending…" and then "✓ Sent to iPhone". At ~20.4–20.6s the camera zooms back out to rest.

1ebgeo-minimal-portfolio-with-games.summary: A single-column, text-led portfolio on a pure white page (#ffffff), shown as a zoomed screen recording: the camera pans and zooms between moments. A left-aligned column (about 470 to 1440 px wide at the 1s framing) holds the name "Nexvyn" in near-black Inter-style sans, the role "Design Engineer" in mid grey, three grey paragraphs with a few black inline links ("reverse-engineer" with a dotted yellow underline, "Twitter", "book a call", "GitHub", an underlined email), then a "projects" section with a handwritten label, list and grid toggle icons, and project rows (name, star count, a large blurred preview card with a radius of about 16 px, a grey caption). A muted speaker icon and a black dot sit fixed in the top-right corner. Blue-grey handwritten notes ("feel free to reach out" with a bracket, "psst, it's a game" with an arrow, and a sheep emoji) sit to the right of the paragraphs. The motion is a run of playful hover reveals. The text fades in from top to bottom (0 to 1s). Hovering the name shows a hand-drawn anime avatar to its left (about 2.5s). Hovering "Design" turns the word into green script and grows a painted flower bouquet on a vine (about 3.5 to 9s; the bouquet blooms between 4.85 and 5.35s). Hovering "GitHub" scribbles over the word, pops up a GitHub mark and a white card with a green contribution grid, "@nexvyn" and "2,341 contributions this year" (about 11.5s). The card then grows a teal pixel-art game frame (12.4s) and expands to a full-screen top-down pixel-art game between 12.8 and 13.55s, with a "BACK TO SITE" HUD, a "NEXVYN" knight, towers and a pond. At about 15.9s the game cross-fades back to the page at the projects section. Hovering a project preview swaps a blurred card for a sharper screenshot (about 20s). Hovering a list row gives it a light grey pill (22.5 to 23s). A black circle wipes the page dark from the right (about 24.5s, with a "Nexvyn prefers light mode" toast) and back. The clip ends on a painted lotus pond that rises in from the bottom (about 26.9 to 30s).

ti5i8b-vercel-agents-homepage-redesign.summary: A Vercel-style hero on a 1482x1080 canvas. A slim nav bar runs along the top (black Vercel triangle at x 127, links Products ▾ / Resources ▾ / Enterprise / Pricing, then three pill buttons on the right: Get a Demo, Log In and a filled Sign Up ending at x 1334). The left column, aligned at x≈127, holds a two-line tight-tracked headline, "Build and run / agents on Vercel" (~56px, y 298–402), a two-line grey subhead and two pill CTAs: a filled "Create an agent" and an outlined "Talk to an expert". The right half shows an isometric 3D cube drawn as a hexagon (box ≈803,347,352,320). It has three rounded rhombus faces, top, lower-left and right, separated by gaps. Six thick black chevron frame segments sit around them, and a faint hexagonal halo and a soft drop shadow sit underneath. A small white Vercel triangle sits on the top face. Above the cube are two chat bubbles joined to it by hairline connectors: a user bubble "@data-agent How did revenue trend last quarter by region?" at the top right, and an agent reply bubble with a small robot avatar circle to its left. Along the bottom, a four-column stat row (4T+, 3×, 1M+, < 5 min; ~56px light-weight numerals at y≈858, two-line grey captions at y≈930) starts at x 126/434/741/1048. Motion: a cursor moves over the cube. The face under the cursor lightens to a soft grey gradient, and an annotation fades in (~200 ms) with a short hairline leader, a bold title and a 3-line grey caption: Connect (bottom-left, ~0.2–1.0s), Sandbox (right, ~1.0–1.7s), eve (top-left, ~1.8–2.4s), Drives (left, ~2.5–3.2s). From ~3.3s nothing is annotated. At ~4.1s the page hard-cuts from light (#f7f7f7 bg, near-black type) to dark (#000 bg, white type, buttons inverted). The cube becomes outline-only: black faces with thin grey stroked edges and outlined frame segments. In dark mode, hovering the lower-left face lights it and brings back Connect (~5.1–5.9s), which then fades as the cursor leaves. The layout never moves; only the hover highlights, annotations, cursor and theme change.

1t92dp-skeuomorphic-image-compressor-mac.summary: A white 1440x1080 canvas with one centred column. At the top sits a skeuomorphic compressor machine (x 425–1016, y 178–408): a warm-grey plastic body with rounded corners, a brushed-steel top deck split into a small left plate and a long control plate. The control plate holds a dark-grey LCD window with a diagonal reflection, a knurled cobalt-blue knob and a small glossy orange-red button. A cream front face sits below the deck, then a long horizontal feed slot. Under the machine is a drop zone: a faint dotted grid (x 445–985, y 455–710) with centred black 22px type "Drop your image here" and grey "or click browse files". Near the bottom is a light-grey capsule (y 924–1004) holding a dark-grey "Compress" pill with a small squeeze icon and a white "Size" pill. A photo card (portrait of a woman with windswept hair against blue sky) rests tilted about -4° at the right (x 1053–1401, y 438–683), with a rounded 16px corner, a small file-icon chip and a large soft shadow. Motion: the cursor grabs the card at ~1.4s; the card lifts and its shadow grows. From 1.9 to 2.6s it is dragged left about 460px onto the drop zone, still tilted. At ~3.1s the card vanishes, the drop-zone text blurs out and the Size pill rolls to "58KB" (digits slide up one by one). At ~3.4s the photo appears flat and square-cornered (x 507–934, y 440–728), wrapped in a translucent white diagonally striped plastic bag hanging from the slot (x 484–956, to y ~790). The Compress pill turns black on hover around 4.2–5.6s. From ~6.6s the bag vacuum-squeezes: its sides pinch into a waist, the photo shrinks to ~356x272 and wrinkles, and the bottom edge turns ragged (done by ~8.5s). Around 10.1–10.7s an orange light runs along the slot and the size rolls from 58KB to "21KB". At ~11.5s the Compress pill becomes a light-grey "Download" pill with a download-tray icon, and that holds to the end.

upmtie-agents-platform-hero.summary: A centred, single-column hero on an off-white page (#fcfcfc). From the top: a small orange outline four-point spark with four short yellow-orange rays (centre ~404,92), a dark sans heading "A faster path to production AI" (~26px, centred at y≈175), and a two-line grey subtitle (~25px, lines at y≈222 and y≈263). Below sits a near-square stage panel (64,337 → 743,1015, fill #fafafa, 1px very light border, tiny notched corners) with a 3px orange-red dot just outside each corner. Centred in the panel at y≈676 is a white fully-rounded terminal pill with a soft drop shadow holding the orange Cloudflare cloud, a grey "$", dark monospace "npm" and orange monospace "i agents" with an orange block cursor. Motion: at 0s the pill is only an ~82px white circle around the cloud; by ~0.45s it has stretched sideways into the full ~378px pill; the command then types out character by character ("n" at 0.5s, "npm i a" at 0.8s, "npm i agen" at 1.0s, "npm i agents" at 1.3s). At ~1.3–1.4s a puff of tiny coloured specks bursts from the middle of the pill, and by ~1.8s it has become a ring of ~40 white circular logo bubbles (AI and tool brands: Google, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral, NVIDIA, Hugging Face, Cloudflare, Zed, Replit-style R and so on) around the pill. From ~1.8s to the end (12.37s) those bubbles fill the whole panel and keep drifting, as if a grab-hand cursor were dragging them, at roughly 150–250 px/s. Bubbles grow and shrink as they move: most are 50–90px, but at any moment a few swell to 150–220px. They are clipped by the panel edges and can slide over the pill. The header, subtitle, panel and pill never move.
